title: Deep GCMT pairs gave no clear extra tensor similarity under regional time shuffles in 1980-2020
abstract: We tested moment tensor similarity in deep earthquake pairs within 200 km and seven days. We used 1,064 Global CMT events with centroid depth greater than 300 km and computed Mw at least 5.5 in 1980-2020. We removed mean similarity in groups defined by year, region, distance and depth. The 106 close pairs had mean residual similarity 0.0246. In 9,999 regional time shuffles, the mean was -0.0001 and the central 95% range was -0.0429 to 0.0413. The upper-tail p-value was 0.1269. Thus this test gave no clear extra similarity. Six checks also gave no clear excess. This does not establish absence or reject triggering. Sparse groups, shared events, centroid errors, catalog selection and the time exchangeability assumption limit inference. The package gives original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an arithmetic audit. External catalog records are excluded.

display.caption: Blue points show observed residual similarity. Gray bars show central 95% time-shuffle ranges. Black marks show shuffle means. These are null ranges, not effect confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Its close deep-pair count result motivated a distinct moment tensor test. We read the signed result. No code or data were copied; catalogs and periods differ.
